subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Caral: The Americas' Oldest City
description: A 60-second lesson on Caral: The Americas' Oldest City.

hook.text: A city in Peru was thriving at the same time as the Egyptian pyramids. It had no pottery, no weapons, and no war.

buildup.text: Caral was built around 2600 BCE, making it the oldest known city in the Americas by a wide margin.

discovery.text: It has six large platform mounds, sunken plazas, and a residential area — but zero evidence of warfare.

twist.text: Archaeologists found quipus — knotted string records — which were thought to have been invented 3,000 years later by the Inca.

climax.text: Caral challenges the idea that civilization requires war. This society built monuments on trade, not conquest.

punchline.text: The oldest American city had pyramids but no army. Peace was its foundation.

quiz.question: What makes Caral unusual compared to other early civilizations?
options: It was built entirely underground to avoid detection
There is zero evidence of warfare — it appears to have been a peaceful society
It was exclusively a religious site with no permanent residents

details.summary: Caral in Peru, dating to about 2600 BCE, is the oldest known city in the Americas. Its pyramids, plazas, and residential areas were built by a civilization that predated the Maya by 2,000 years. Remarkably, Caral developed without pottery, writing, or apparently any warfare evidence.
details.whyItMatters: Caral proves that complex civilizations in the Americas are far older than previously believed. Its development without war or pottery challenges assumptions about what conditions are necessary for urbanization.
takeaways: The oldest known city in the Americas, dating to about 2600 BCE
Predates Maya civilization by approximately 2,000 years
Developed without pottery, writing, or evidence of warfare

faq.question: How was Caral's age established?
faq.answer: Radiocarbon dating of reed bags used to carry building materials consistently produced dates around 2600 BCE. These dates were initially controversial because they predated all known American civilizations by millennia. Multiple laboratories confirmed the results, and the dating is now accepted.

faq.question: How did Caral's society function without pottery or writing?
faq.answer: They used gourds and woven baskets instead of pottery. Quipu (knotted string) may have served record-keeping functions. Their economy was based on fishing and irrigation agriculture, trading dried fish for inland crops.
